speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to your consultation. I understand you have knee pain after recently increasing your physical activity; to help you, please describe exactly where the pain is located and what kind of activity triggered it. Also, did you experience a loud popping sound or notice any swelling immediately after the event?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the details; given your history of volleyball with repetitive pivoting and the recent onset of worsening pain, I need to know if you felt a specific "pop" during the injury and if there is any visible swelling or instability now. Please also confirm if you can still bear weight on the affected leg.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints).

The pain location you described—medial aspect of the tibia inferior to the patella—is classic for this condition, especially given your recent increase in activity and history of being advised on weight loss. Since the pain has been worsening, I need to confirm if it is localized to a specific tender point along the tibia or if it involves the joint space itself. Can you press on the shinbone and tell me if you feel a sharp, pinpoint tenderness?
